decisions: An array has one owning Mantle Device/domain; many nodes in multiple graphs may reference it.
A Group contains operation nodes, not adapted arrays/devices; no recording-device wrapper or returned Group alias.
Ordinary eager numerical methods keep Julia signatures, without an extra public device argument.
The separate recorded-call entry explicitly names Graph/Group and a supported function.
One shared Mantle/GPUArrays-style operation layer serves eager and recorded calls and owns device-capability dispatch; backend algorithm duplication is forbidden.
Known operation definitions/recipes supply shared validation, effects, returns, candidate materialization and resource management; arbitrary Julia capture is not promised.
Return contracts are explicit per operation definition: mul! returns C; recorded Array returns a typed future; neither ! nor a universal-future heuristic determines this.
Array(a) is standard blocking eager conversion; call!(target,Array,a) declares a snapshot; Readback(previous_future) only requests its next execution. No separate public eager Readback(array).
Actual CPU work during replay uses explicit hostcall! staging/host cuts; unsupported call! never falls back to it or eager execution.

The core selector intersects enabled hardware/compiler capability, precision/layout/shape/alias/workspace and recording/control requirements, then compares eligible candidates using measured evidence.
Eager calls materialize immediately; graph compile materializes/reselects retained recipes; replay uses baked choices without probing/tuning.
KA.get_backend(a) stays the owning Mantle Device; ordinary host length/size queries synchronize and return snapshots, never a recording target or hidden graph provenance.

Target-aware consumer graph builders such as PrintSim.step!(group,world,state,dt) are called directly during construction; no call! adapter or operation registration is required for their composition.
A recorded window screenshot uses call!(presenting_graph,Array,win) and the common future lifecycle; Array(win) rejects instead of blocking on unsubmitted future work.
Ordinary device-array destination sum! supplies GPU-resident reduction results; no new public scalar handle or mandatory replacement of PrintSim world_dot!.
Capacity is a usable allocation bound/backing requirement for nonresident state; descriptor publication requires actual backing and excludes virtual spare.

Canonical payload byte identity/ownership and logical-header metadata are distinct; independent imported headers keep their own shapes/capacity units while data hazards/readonly/lease restrictions remain shared (F123).

No public Device(Graph/Group) constructor/query overload: it was an unneeded ownership convenience retained after removing recording-device wrappers. Core resolves ownership internally; recording explicitly names Graph/Group.

User explicitly selects hostcall!(target,f,args;writes) for replay-time CPU callbacks, replacing dispatch!/hostcall! syntax. mul! documentation now expands recipe/candidate/materialize/kernel hookups with core-owned selection.
Supported consumer API is explicitly exported or declared public; implementation helpers use neither. Cache trimming is private core/test maintenance.

Particle compaction is an illustrative application graph builder, not a new Mantle API. Explicit array-backing trimming is deferred; shrink retains capacity. AS compact! remains a separate scene-storage operation.
